_doc: Linux (`platform: linux`) entries: the same game facts as the Windows files, located in the
ELF modules of the *other* build (steam.inf ClientVersion 2000908, staged with
`stagebins.py --linux --unshare` from the cs2-home podman volume into target/game-bins-linux).
Addresses are vaddrs (image_base 0). The game's own C++ symbols are hidden (.dynsym holds only
libstdc++/libc++/tier0-utility `_ZTV` symbols), so a vtable here is located through the code that
uses it, not through RTTI or a `_ZTV` symbol: sigs/README.md 'Linux binaries', 'itanium_vtable'.
The CClientInput / CCSGOInput entries are for build 2000930 only (libclient.so there, staged from the
client image's cache): the destructors that store the address points are the locators, the two secondary
tables are the CCSGOInput address point plus a displacement read from the binary (s2sdk-types RE8).
Nothing in this file has a `bridge` macro: the bridge is Windows-only and the gate ignores these.

CG_ENTITY_CHUNKS.via: libclient.so!0xf0cdc7 (mov r14,[rip+0x36cb932]) inside the entity-identity lookup at 0xf0cde1-0xf0ce05: movzwl (%rcx),%eax; shr $0x9,%r11; and $0x3f,%r11d; mov (%r14,%r11,8),%r11 (the chunk-pointer array); and $0x1ff,%eax; imul $0x70,%rax,%rax (CEntityIdentity stride 112); add %rax,%r11; cmp %r9d,0x10(%r11) (the handle at identity+0x10). Same geometry as the Windows entry (512 identities per chunk, 112-byte identity), reached from a different code path
CG_ENTITY_CHUNKS.notes: pointer to the CEntityIdentity chunk-pointer array (512 identities per chunk = 1<<9, mask 0x1FF, stride 112 = 0x70); the lookup also clamps the chunk index with & 0x3F (64 chunks = 1<<15 identities, the 0x8000 index bound of the Windows notes). Not a bridge entry: the Linux consumer is s2sdk-probe, not the DLL

CG_INPUT_PTR.via: libclient.so!0x18f342d in CSource2Client::CreateMove (0x18f3340, entry 22 of the CSource2Client table at address point 0x44ecdc0, _ZTI14CSource2Client just before it; Windows twin client!0x180B7B980 = ??_7CSource2Client@@6B@ slot 22): lea rax,[rip+g_pInput]; ... mov rdi,[rax]; mov byte [r14],1; mov rax,[rdi]; call [rax+28h] (CCSGOInput entry 5, the Itanium twin of the Windows [rax+20h]); target 0x4682620, a .data qword initialised to the static CCSGOInput object 0x494a060 (constructed by 0x1ae6110, which stores the address point 0x4513600)
CG_INPUT_PTR.notes: g_pInput (pointer to the static CCSGOInput); Linux twin of client.json CG_INPUT_PTR (client!0x2233d10). PIC code loads it as lea+mov, so the locator resolves the lea. Not a bridge entry: the Linux consumer is the Rust plugin

CCONST_IDENTITY_CHUNK_BITS.via: libclient.so!0xf0cde7 (shr $0x9,%r11; and $0x3f,%r11d; mov (%r14,%r11,8),%r11) in the same identity lookup as CG_ENTITY_CHUNKS: the identity index is split into a chunk index (index >> bits) and an in-chunk offset (index & 0x1FF); the `disp` step reads the shift immediate (0x09) out of the instruction
CCONST_IDENTITY_CHUNK_BITS.notes: CEntityIdentity chunk geometry on Linux: 512 identities per chunk = 1<<9, mask 0x1FF - the same value as CCONST_IDENTITY_CHUNK_BITS on Windows build 2000930 (mcp_bridge_game.inc:124-133). The stride multiply at 0xf0ce01 is imul 0x70 = 112, also the Windows identity size

CCONST_IDENTITY_STRIDE.via: libclient.so!0xf0ce01 (imul rax, rax, 0x70) inside the entity-identity lookup at 0xf0cde1-0xf0ce0c - the same lookup as CG_ENTITY_CHUNKS / CCONST_IDENTITY_CHUNK_BITS: movzwl (%rcx),%eax; mov %rax,%r11; shr $0x9,%r11; and $0x3f,%r11d; mov (%r14,%r11,8),%r11; and $0x1ff,%eax; imul $0x70,%rax,%rax; add %rax,%r11; cmp %r9d,0x10(%r11) (the handle compare at identity+0x10). The sig is anchored on the imul and the `disp` step reads its immediate (0x70) out of the instruction, exactly as CCONST_IDENTITY_CHUNK_BITS reads the shr immediate
CCONST_IDENTITY_STRIDE.notes: CEntityIdentity stride on Linux = 0x70 = 112 - the size the Windows identity lookups scale the in-chunk index by too (client.json CCONST_IDENTITY_STRIDE) and the IR's itanium sizeof(CEntityIdentity), the number sdkcheck.py --platform linux compares this entry against (row id:CEntityIdentity-stride). The `and $0x1ff,%eax; imul $0x70,%rax,%rax; add %rax,%r11; cmp %r9d,0x10(%r11)` byte sequence occurs once in the module (measured), so the sig is unique - resolve --strict proves it. Not a bridge entry: the Linux consumer is s2sdk-probe, not the DLL

CClientInput.via: libclient.so 0x18f1fd0: the complete-object destructor, which begins with push rbp, lea rax,[rip+vtable] (the CClientInput vtable address point) and stores it as the object's first qword. No `_ZTV` symbol is exported for the class
CClientInput.notes: CClientInput, the base class of CCSGOInput: a single Itanium table, offset-to-top 0; the Windows build's table has 33 entries (s2sdk-types RE8 section 3.1)

VTLEN_CClientInput.via: libclient.so address point 0x44eda00: 34 .text slot pointers up to the next table's header
VTLEN_CClientInput.notes: Itanium length of CClientInput, compared by sdkcheck.py with the generated CClientInput (the destructor's two entries and 32 virtuals), RE8 section 4

CCSGOInput.via: libclient.so 0x1ace670: the complete-object destructor, which begins with push rbp, lea rax,[rip+vtable] (the CCSGOInput vtable address point), stores it as the object's first qword and the IInputHandler table (address point + a displacement that is masked in the pattern, 0x148 here) at +0xB88, then compares dword [rdi+disp] with 0x3FFFFFFF (disp masked: 0xBDC on 2000930, 0xBEC on 2000933). No `_ZTV` symbol is exported for the class
